description: This bar chart illustrates the accuracy values associated with different data augmentation techniques applied to a BERT model. The horizontal axis displays the categories of data augmentation, labeled “embedding,” “1st layer,” “random layers,” “random +R2,” “random +permute,” “random,” “+B2,” “+L2,” “+R2 +permute,” and “unperturbed,” arranged alphabetically. The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy,” represents a linear scale ranging from 70 to 95, with tick marks at intervals of 5. Each category is represented by a single bar, with colors varying between teal, light blue, green, and red. The shortest bar corresponds to the “random” category, with an approximate accuracy of 72, while the tallest bar corresponds to the “unperturbed” category, reaching an accuracy of approximately 84. The bars generally increase in height from “embedding” (approximately 82) through “random +permute” (approximately 82) to “unperturbed,” with some fluctuations in height between categories. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
